description:
FOUND s499a (Opus, 2026-09-27, measurement only), ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/REPORT.md.

PROFILE (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/profiles/moo-class.txt, sb-sprof :cpu): 89.3 % of the warm run is under pcl:p-eval -> %p-eval-1 -> sb-c:compile-in-lexenv: SBCL's native compiler (constraint propagation, ir1-optimize, regalloc) compiling the code Moo/Sub::Quote generate by string eval, EVERY RUN (the eval cache holds text; #1410 is the fasl half, blocked).
EXPERIMENT (nothing shipped): `(proclaim '(optimize (compilation-speed 3) (speed 0) (space 1) (debug 0) (safety 1)))` injected at start-up (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/bin/exp-cspeed.lisp; only runtime compiles are affected -- every fasl is already compiled).  Warm, interleaved ctl/exp/ctl2, min of 3:
  moo-class 2.653 -> 0.543 s;  moo-objs N=1 1.622 -> 0.316;  moo-objs N=20000 3.089 -> 1.772 (saved 1.316 s = the same as at N=1, so the per-object cost did not move);  json-rt 2.97 -> 2.89;  1000 x eval "2 + 3" 0.888 -> 0.787.
  Everyday corpus K=1 (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/exp-cspeed-everyday.log): stdout identical 101/101; the savings sit in the four eval-using programs (moo-class -2.15 s, stat-fh -0.135, JSON-PP -0.065, json-pp -0.043) = about 2.4 s of the corpus's 10.3 s warm total.
THE ALTERNATIVE #2191 NAMES, measured beside it (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/exp-interpret.log): sb-ext:*evaluator-mode* :interpret saves MORE on set-up (moo-class -88 %, moo-objs N=1 -90 %) but makes hot eval-generated code slower (moo-objs N=20000 +38 %) -- a policy binding has no such cliff.
FIX SHAPE (a sketch, not a design): bind the policy (sb-ext:restrict-compiler-policy or a `(declare (optimize ...))`-carrying wrapper) around the EVAL in %p-eval-1 only; measure which quality carries it (the three-way split was not taken).  Relation: #1410 (eval fasl) removes the compile entirely for repeated texts; #2191 (per-execution recompile); this is the cheap step before either.
subject: PERF: a string eval's CL is compiled at SBCL's DEFAULT policy -- binding a cheap policy around the eval cuts Moo class set-up ~1.3 s per run (moo-class 2.69 -> 0.54 s, -80 %) with the per-object cost unchanged
